data.text:
F24 is fixed at records 108 and 110, and verified independently of the implementer that
wrote it.

## The RED is the point of this round

F22's round corrected a false reason and added an assertion that passed on its first run.
That is why its twin survived in the sentence next door and had to be found again. This
round encoded the claim as behaviour instead: put the restricting key in place inside a
rolled-back transaction, require `delete from public.tenants` to be refused, and let it
fail. It did, with `erasingTheTenant: accepted` against an expected `23503`. A test that
grepped the migration for a phrase would have gone red just as reliably and proved
nothing about the database.

## What was checked after the fix

The correction changes why restrict is excluded, not whether, so the thing worth proving
is that the exclusion still bites. A restricting key was planted on
`claims_credited_by_settlement_line_id_fkey` and the suite was run: it exits 1 and names
the key, with the corrected message, "1 foreign keys refuse a delete of the parent
outright, so the row each points at cannot be removed or re-ingested while it stands".
The old message said "which a tenant's erasure is", which was the false half stated as
fact at the moment the assertion fired. The database was reset afterwards and the suite
is green at 94.

## One correction that went further than F24 named, and why

`rls.test.ts:717` carried both halves of the error: the restrict claim this round owns,
and a set-null claim that is F22's, saying an erasure would fail the not-null constraint
on the way through. The two were one sentence. The implementer could not correct the half
it was asked for without rewriting the whole, so it wrote both correctly and said so. That
is the right call and it is recorded here rather than left inside a rewritten sentence:
the change is larger than F24's name, and a reviewer should see that it is.

## Found and not fixed

- The ticket's `## Outcome` does not repeat the erasure claim about restrict. It says only
  "Nothing became restrict, and a test refuses one", which is whether and not why, and is
  still true. Nothing to correct there.
- F25 is untouched: the unreproduced failing run, and `seen.erased_tenants` still growing
  on every run because the tests that seed and erase outside a transaction leave their
  tombstones behind.

## The method this round argues for

Three of the five findings of record 88 were claims that had never been run: F22, F24 and
the set-null half of the same `rls.test.ts` sentence. In each case the code was right and
the stated reason was not, and in each case the way to catch it was to write the claim as
a test and watch it fail. A comment cannot be wrong in a way anything notices; an
assertion can. Where a migration explains itself, the explanation is worth an assertion
whenever it makes a claim about behaviour, and that is the general lesson of F22 and F24
rather than anything about foreign keys.

F19 to F24 are now all fixed. F25 is open.
